purpose: Expected (row, subject) records and verdicts for the native-entry campaign. 'repaired' subjects must conform; 'violates' broken subjects must violate the claim they name; 'conforms' lists subjects that conform by design and carry a reason. 'baseline' classifies the incumbent product (the pre-repair revision, built as its own frozen tree) under the same claims: class 'observed' needs one baseline record whose raw verdict is classified fails (violated a claim) or already-correct (held every claim) and is never required to fail; class 'rejected-premise' carries the reason and the missing mechanism and must have no record. A row with no baseline entry is unclassified and fails reconciliation. Resolution order: the running platform's exact row (platforms.<name>.rows), then the base exact row, then the first matching pattern of the row's family, then the family default. This file is a subject of every campaign: digest it before and after.
domain: aarch64-apple-darwin host receipts only; they qualify neither GNU/Linux nor Rust 1.85

linux.reason: The base plan's expectations were frozen on aarch64-apple-darwin. A platform row replaces the base expectation for that exact row where the kernel's behaviour differs, each with its reason; the 153 row identities are never changed or dropped.

E03__disposition=ignore.reason: Linux: an ignored SIGCHLD disposition is itself the no-zombie state (a wait fails with ECHILD once the children are gone) and execve preserves SIG_IGN while clearing action flags (flush_signal_handlers, v6.18), so skipping the worker repair loses the worker's wait. The Darwin premise (skip-repair is already waitable because exec clears the flag) does not exist on this kernel; this row is a failing discriminator of its own, and the E04 worker row stays independent.

E04__boundary=raw-executable-entry__stat.reason: Linux: executable entry always sees action flags cleared (flush_signal_handlers, v6.18), so SA_NOCLDWAIT cannot reach it by inheritance. The verdict asserts the observed flag is clear after the harness read back its pre-exec injection (default plus SA_NOCLDWAIT, confirmed before exec, or the spawn is refused); it never relabels the private injection as inheritance. No repair is claimed and no mutant exists. The row keeps its Darwin spelling as its identity.

linux-emulated.reason: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu under QEMU user-mode emulation on an aarch64 Linux kernel. Rows an emulator cannot reproduce are listed with their reason and control rather than reconciled; every other row must reconcile to the platform expectations of 'linux'. Emulated receipts qualify nothing about an x86-64 kernel.

E04__boundary=worker__state=private-defa.reason: QEMU's user-mode emulator installs its own host signal handler for a guest's SIGCHLD and does not forward SA_NOCLDWAIT to the host kernel, so the private default-plus-SA_NOCLDWAIT state this row injects has no effect: the skip-repair subject's waits still succeed. That is a property of this emulator, not a statement about an x86-64 kernel.
E04__boundary=worker__state=private-defa.control: scripts/native-linux/emulation-probe.c, one source built for both targets: nocldwait_wait is ECHILD natively on aarch64 Linux and the child's exit status under the emulator, while sigign_wait is ECHILD in both.

spec.reason: Negative control: with no pending signal the entry-blocked-pending mutant is not discriminating, so it conforms by design.
Observation of whether the flag reaches executable entry; no repair is claimed and no mutant exists. The measured flag state is in the record's note.
Real-signal-death control: a successful raise cannot report afterwards, so there is no ignore-the-failure mutant for it.

baseline.reason: The pair is the policy refusal and a failed final mask restore. On a policy refusal the incumbent settles the selection failure without restoring the signal mask at all: its handled signals are blocked only by the pre-launch `block_and_check`, which a refusal never reaches, so the final restore the row faults is not performed on this path. The same fixture selecting the site on a refusal reaches nothing, and reaches the site on the spawn-ENOENT path (hosted by F05).
baseline.missing: a final signal-mask restore on the selection-refusal path (the incumbent neither blocks nor restores the mask there)

baseline.reason: The row's faulted operation is an observation that never answers while the child must already be gone, reached through a failed Started check and ended by an absolute error-settlement deadline. The incumbent enters no error path for a child that is merely still running: an always-running observation is its ordinary supervision loop, a documented stall the caller closes, so there is no settlement to observe and no deadline for the claim to read. (Its observation and reap failures, which it does handle, are the other six S02 rows and are hosted.)
baseline.missing: an absolute error-settlement deadline over a still-running child (the incumbent's error paths are an observation failure and a reap failure only)

baseline.reason: The row faults one operation of the repaired common finalisation's signal snapshot: the final handled-signal block, the pending-set query behind it, or the TERM membership read of that set, taken after the work and before the mask is released. The incumbent has no such snapshot: its only block and pending query are the pre-launch `block_and_check`, before the managed child exists, and its finalisation restores the mask directly. The same fixture selecting each of these sites on the incumbent reaches none of them, on all three outcomes, and the launch runs to its end.

baseline.reason: The row faults the worker-side watching establishment (the SIGCHLD action query, or the default-action repair that clears default plus no-child-wait) before the worker is spawned. The incumbent's worker admission performs neither: its worker module never names SIGCHLD, so under the row's state the worker is spawned and later waited unwatched. The same fixture selecting each of the three sites on the incumbent reaches none of them and the worker is admitted; the failure that absence causes (ECHILD at the worker's wait) is E04's worker row, already recorded.
baseline.missing: worker-side child-watching establishment: a SIGCHLD action query and a default-action repair before the worker is spawned

baseline.reason: The row faults the runner's default-action repair of default plus no-child-wait. The incumbent's runner repairs SIGCHLD only when the inherited disposition is an ignore (`SIG_IGN`) and performs no repair at all for default plus no-child-wait, so under the row's state there is no repair operation to omit or to report failed. A control on the same role sees the repair site reached for an ignored disposition and not reached for default plus no-child-wait; the query row of the same boundary is hosted. The failure this absence causes (ECHILD at the managed wait) is E04's managed row, already recorded.
baseline.missing: the independent no-child-wait repair of a default SIGCHLD disposition (the incumbent repairs only an ignored one)

E03.reason: Darwin exec clears the private no-child-wait flag, so skipping the worker repair still confirms both waits; the E04 worker row is the independent failing discriminator in this domain. No baseline failure is invented.

E05.reason: Positive row: the frozen contract names a child-status discriminator only for the PTY-VINTR after-handoff row.

baseline.reason: Every S01 row faults one stop attempt of the settlement that follows a failed Started check, and its one named claim reads that attempt's retained report. The incumbent's Started is the infallible observer(LaunchEvent::Started), a `&mut dyn FnMut(LaunchEvent)`, so no check can fail, and its stops (kill, Process::signal, Process::kill_group) return nothing and ignore the failure on purpose. There is no operation report channel, so the fact the claim reads cannot exist; it is recorded as the reason, not as a failure the incumbent was never observed to commit.
baseline.missing: checked stop operations with a per-attempt report channel (and the fallible post-spawn start check that leads to them)
